name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Glenn Thompson running with large financial edge
Democratic challenger minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
model.rationale: Thompson holds a deep structural advantage in an R+19 district, has out-raised Bilger more than thirteen-to-one, and markets give him roughly a 96% chance of winning. No polls or expert ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals-based forecast.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected incumbent scandal would be the only plausible path to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North-central Pennsylvania's 15th District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Glenn Thompson is seeking another term with the full advantages of incumbency. He has raised about $1.85 million and holds over $800,000 in cash, while Democratic challenger Ray Bilger has raised under $150,000 with no visible outside support. No independent polls or expert ratings track the race, but prediction markets price Thompson as roughly a 96% favorite.

The district's R+19 partisan lean, Thompson's incumbency, and his overwhelming financial edge all point the same direction. A Democratic win would require a dramatic, unforeseen shift in the political environment; the realistic range of outcomes runs from a comfortable Thompson win to a landslide.
